summary: The change adds a check in FormatterDescriptor.TryCreate to skip abstract types implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T>, preventing them from being counted as formatters. This fixes the root cause of issues #2017 (MsgPack013 and MsgPack009 for abstract formatters). All four requirements are satisfied: the new test passes on head and fails on base without the fix, confirming the change addresses the issue; the full suite shows no regressions; and non-abstract formatters continue to be discovered as before.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: The analyzer skips abstract types in TryCreate (line 221-225 head), so abstract classes implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T> are not counted as formatters, preventing MsgPack013. The new test AbstractFormatterDoesNotAttractAttention passes on head and fails on base without the fix.

Abstract implementations are excluded from formatter counting (TryCreate returns false for abstract types), so two abstract formatters for the same type cannot trigger MsgPack009. The test AbstractFormatterDoesNotAttractAttention has two abstract classes both implementing IMessagePackFormatter<object> and passes on head, confirming no MsgPack009 is reported.
